title: Grothendieck spectral sequence for a composite
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. For a scheme $T$ let $T_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\Lambda_T$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $\Lambda$ on it [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)=\Mod(\Lambda_T)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $f_*$, $h_*$, $(hf)_*$ be the direct images on these categories [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and, for $u\in\{f,h,hf\}$, let $R^qu_*$ be the right derived functors of the left exact functor $u_*$ on $\Mod(-,\Lambda)$, computed by injective resolutions in $\Mod(-,\Lambda)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Then for every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ there is a first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence $(E_r^{p,q},d_r)_{r\ge2}$ in $\Mod(Z_{\Et},\Lambda)$, with $d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$, $d_r\circ d_r=0$ and $E_{r+1}\cong\ker d_r/\operatorname{im}d_r$, such that

$$
 E_2^{p,q}=R^ph_*\bigl(R^qf_*F\bigr)\ \ (p,q\ge0),\qquad E_2^{p,q}=0\ \text{otherwise},
$$

converging to $R^{p+q}(hf)_*F$ in the following sense: for $r>\max(p,q+1)$ one has $E_{r+1}^{p,q}=E_r^{p,q}=:E_\infty^{p,q}$, and each $H^n=R^n(hf)_*F$ ($n\ge0$) carries a finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] $H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq F^1H^n\supseteq\dots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0$ with $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. The spectral sequence, the filtrations and these isomorphisms are functorial in $F$. No hypothesis on $F$ is needed. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ the categories $\Mod(T_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$ are the categories $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], so the statement holds for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$, and then $R^qu_*$ are the higher direct images $\mathcal H^q(Ru_*F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text: *The categories and the functors.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], applied to $T=X,Y,Z$, the categories $\mathcal A=\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $\mathcal B=\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $\mathcal C=\Mod(Z_{\Et},\Lambda)$ are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]; in particular they have enough injectives, so the right derived functors of the statement are defined. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (with $R=\Lambda$), for each of $u=f,h,hf$ the direct image $u_*$ on $\Lambda$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is right adjoint to the inverse image $u^{-1}$ on $\Lambda$-module sheaves. A right adjoint preserves all limits, in particular finite products and kernels, so $f_*:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $h_*:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ and $(hf)_*:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ are additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Hence $(f_*,h_*)$ is a composable pair in the sense of [def-sp-composite-acyclicity].

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0734 (label lemma-relative-Leray), proof: 'a Grothendieck spectral sequence for composition of functors'; Derived Categories, Lemma 015M (label lemma-compose-derived-functors), hypotheses: F, G left exact, A, B with enough injectives (literature/stacks-project/derived.tex)

proof.text: *The composite.* There is a natural isomorphism of functors $(hf)_*\cong h_*\circ f_*:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$. Indeed, for $W\to Z$ etale, $(h_*f_*F)(W)=F\bigl((W\times_ZY)\times_YX\bigr)$ and $((hf)_*F)(W)=F(W\times_ZX)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. In the diagram formed by the cartesian square $(W\times_ZY)\times_YX\to X$ over $W\times_ZY\to Y$ on top of the cartesian square $W\times_ZY\to Y$ over $W\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the pasting lemma [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] shows that the outer rectangle is cartesian, i.e. $(W\times_ZY)\times_YX$ with its maps to $X$ and to $W$ is a fibre product of $hf$ and $W\to Z$; so there is a unique isomorphism $(W\times_ZY)\times_YX\cong W\times_ZX$ over $X$ and over $W$. It is an isomorphism of objects of $X_{\Et}$, natural in $W$ by uniqueness, so the induced maps on sections of $F$ are $\Lambda$-linear, compatible with restriction, and natural in $F$. Consequently the right derived functors agree: $R^n(hf)_*F\cong R^n(h_*\circ f_*)F$, naturally in $F$, both being $\mathcal H^n$ of the image of one injective resolution of $F$ under isomorphic functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0734 (label lemma-relative-Leray): the composition $g\circ f$ of morphisms of ringed topoi, whose direct image is $g_*\circ f_*$

proof.text: *$f_*$ sends injectives to $h_*$-acyclics.* Let $I$ be an injective object of $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives] $f_*I$ is an injective object of $\mathcal B$. An injective object $J$ of $\mathcal B$ is $h_*$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic]: the complex $J$ concentrated in degree $0$ is an injective resolution of $J$, so $R^qh_*(J)=\mathcal H^q(h_*J[0])=0$ for $q>0$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Hence $f_*I$ is $h_*$-acyclic, i.e. $f_*$ sends injectives to $h_*$-acyclics [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. (This is the acyclicity hypothesis of the Grothendieck spectral sequence; it concerns the injective objects of $\mathcal A$ only, and no hypothesis on $F$ is needed. In particular it is not the condition that $f_*F$ be $h_*$-acyclic, which the imported step mistakenly attributed to the statement.)

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0730 (label lemma-pushforward-injective-flat): for flat f, f_* of an injective O-module is injective (here the ringed-site morphism (X_et, Lambda_X) -> (Y_et, Lambda_Y) is flat since u^{-1}Lambda_Y = Lambda_X); Derived Categories, Lemma 015M (label lemma-compose-derived-functors), condition (1)

proof.text: *The spectral sequence.* By steps 1 and 3, [thm-sp-grothendieck] applies to the composable pair $(f_*,h_*)$ and the object $F$ of $\mathcal A$: there is a first-quadrant spectral sequence, functorial in $F$, with $E_2^{p,q}=R^ph_*(R^qf_*F)$, converging to $R^{p+q}(h_*\circ f_*)F$ with the image filtration [def-sp-image-filtration] in the sense of [def-sp-convergence]. Its construction (proof of [thm-sp-grothendieck]) is: an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in $\mathcal A$, a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $C^{\bullet,\bullet}$ of $f_*I^\bullet$ in $\mathcal B$, the first-quadrant double complex $D^{p,q}=h_*C^{p,q}$ in $\mathcal C$, and the spectral sequence of the filtration of $\operatorname{Tot}D$ by the first degree. By step 2 the abutment $R^{p+q}(h_*\circ f_*)F$ is $R^{p+q}(hf)_*F$, naturally in $F$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 015N (label lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence) with its proof and the remark after it: for an object A, E_2^{p,q} = R^pG(R^qF(A)) converging to R^{p+q}(G o F)(A), bounded, with a finite filtration on each abutment; Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0734 (literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex)

proof.text: *Convergence made explicit.* Since $R^q$ vanishes in negative degrees and $D$ lies in the first quadrant, $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, hence $E_r^{p,q}=0$ there for all $r\ge2$ (subquotients). If $r>q+1$ the differential $d_r$ leaving $(p,q)$ lands in $E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$ with $q-r+1<0$, so it is $0$; if $r>p$ the differential arriving at $(p,q)$ starts at $E_r^{p-r,q+r-1}$ with $p-r<0$, so it is $0$. Hence $E_{r+1}^{p,q}=E_r^{p,q}$ for $r>\max(p,q+1)$, and this stable value is the $E_\infty^{p,q}=Z_\infty/B_\infty$ of [def-sp-convergence] (the $Z_r$, $B_r$ being constant from that $r$ on). The filtration of $H^n=H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ is the image filtration $F^pH^n=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^p\operatorname{Tot}D)\to H^n)$ [def-sp-image-filtration] with $(F^p\operatorname{Tot}D)^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}D^{i,n-i}$; as $D^{i,n-i}=0$ for $i>n$ and $F^0\operatorname{Tot}D=\operatorname{Tot}D$, this gives $F^{n+1}H^n=0$ and $F^0H^n=H^n$, so the filtration is finite [def-sp-filtration], and convergence [def-sp-convergence] gives $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. Transported along the isomorphism $H^n\cong R^n(hf)_*F$ of step 4, this is the convergence stated. All constructions are functorial in $F$ by step 4.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 015N (label lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence): 'this spectral sequence is bounded, converges to H^*(R(G o F)(X)), and induces a finite filtration on each H^n'

proof.text: *The abelian case.* For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ the constant sheaf $\mathbf Z_T$ acts on every abelian sheaf in exactly one way, through locally constant integers, and every morphism of abelian sheaves is $\mathbf Z_T$-linear, so the forgetful functor $\Mod(T_{\Et},\mathbf Z)\to\Ab(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] is an isomorphism of categories commuting with the direct images, which are given by the same formula on sections [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; so steps 1--5 give the spectral sequence for every abelian sheaf $F$. The derived functors $R^qu_*F$ used there are computed by an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$; by [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] (part 2, in the Grothendieck abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian] for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$) the bounded-below complex of injectives $I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution of $F[0]$ and $\mathcal H^q(Ru_*F)=\mathcal H^q(u_*I^\bullet)=R^qu_*F$, which identifies them with the higher direct images of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] (defined through K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]).

split_report.summary: Rewritten from Stacks 0734 (relative Leray) via 015M/015N, with 0730 for the acyclicity. Statement: coefficient category made explicit (sheaves of Lambda_T-modules on the small etale sites, Lambda a commutative ring; Lambda = Z gives abelian sheaves, with R^q identified with def-weil-pbc-direct-image's), convergence made explicit in the form lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse and composition-stability step 7 use (finite filtration 0 = F^{n+1} in F^0 = R^n(hf)_*F, gr = E_infty, E_infty = E_r for r > max(p, q+1)). Fixed the inconsistency: the old step spoke of a hypothesis 'f_*F is h_*-acyclic'; the hypothesis of the Grothendieck spectral sequence is that f_* sends injectives to h_*-acyclics, which holds by lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives, so no hypothesis on F. Dropped from the statement: the base-change compatibility clause (neither user, prop-weil-pbc-composition-stability step 7 nor lemma-weil-pbc-cancellation step 6, uses it; it is thm-sp-grothendieck-base-change if ever needed) and the unused clause on bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology. Dropped thm-sp-grothendieck-base-change, def-sp-etale-dictionary (only covers Ab(X_et), not needed: steps 1-5 make the substitution directly) from the dependencies. thm-sp-grothendieck requires Grothendieck abelian categories (def-sp-composite-acyclicity): new node lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian supplies this for Mod(T_et, Lambda). Underived (hf)_* = h_* f_* written out via the pasting lemma. Mathlib: no Grothendieck spectral sequence (SpectralObject machinery only), three kinds of search recorded.

reviewed.note: acyclicity hypothesis clarified (f_* preserves injectives), convergence stated in the form the users need, unused clauses dropped; thm-sp-grothendieck and lem-sp-kinjective-computes (sk-prop-av-pqf-finite) accepted as tool uses; 1 new node

lean.statement: theorem exists_module_grothendieck_spectralSequence (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : let A := Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) let C := Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) let fStar := lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f let hStar := lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) h let hfStar := lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (f ≫ h) ∃ E : E₂CohomologicalSpectralSequence (A ⥤ C), (∀ p q : ℕ, Nonempty ((E.page 2).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)) ≅ fStar.rightDerived q ⋙ hStar.rightDerived p)) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 ∨ q < 0 → IsZero ((E.page 2).X (p, q))) ∧ (∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (p q : ℕ), max (p : ℤ) ((q : ℤ) + 1) < r → Nonempty ((E.page (r + 1)).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)) ≅ (E.page r hr).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)))) ∧ ∃ filtration : ∀ n : ℕ, DecreasingFiltration (hfStar.rightDerived n), (∀ n : ℕ, (filtration n).step 0 = ⊤ ∧ IsZero ((filtration n).step ((n : ℤ) + 1) : A ⥤ C)) ∧ ∀ (n p : ℕ), p ≤ n → ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 2 ≤ r), max (p : ℤ) (((n - p : ℕ) : ℤ) + 1) < r → Nonempty ((filtration n).gradedPiece (p : ℤ) ≅ (E.page r hr).X ((p : ℤ), ((n - p : ℕ) : ℤ)))
